findings.heading: Geoms
findings.proposition: The English says ggplot2 itself contains over 40 geoms and that many FURTHER geoms are created by fans; the Turkish says the 40-plus geoms in ggplot2 were created by volunteers/fans, and drops the existence of additional community geoms.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader believes ggplot2's built-in geoms are community contributions, and does not learn that a large extra set of geoms exists outside the package, so they will not look for extension geoms at the linked gallery.

findings.heading: Groups
findings.proposition: The English states that using only group = inside aes() will NOT create a legend; the Turkish states that it WILL also create a new legend.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader who wants a legend uses group = alone, gets no legend, and cannot tell whether the plot or their code is wrong.

findings.heading: Modify theme
findings.proposition: The English lists the literal values legend.position accepts as "bottom", "top", "left" and "right"; the Turkish lists them as "alt", "üst", "sol" and "sağ", which ggplot2 does not accept and which the adjacent chunk contradicts (it uses legend.position = "bottom").
findings.reader_consequence: The reader writes legend.position = "alt" and the plot fails or ignores the setting, with no hint in the text that the value must stay in English.

findings.heading: Histograms
findings.proposition: The English instructs the reader to set y = after_stat(density); the Turkish writes y = after_stat(yoğunluk), while the code chunk immediately below (tr 807, 812) uses after_stat(density).
findings.reader_consequence: The reader copies after_stat(yoğunluk) and gets an error, because no such statistic exists; the same line tells them to use the syntax exactly, so they have no reason to suspect the translated word.

findings.heading: Labels
findings.proposition: The English says the caption shows the maximum hospitalisation DATE in the linelist; the Turkish says it shows the maximum hospital stay DURATION, which the adjacent code (max(linelist$date_hospitalisation)) contradicts.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader misreads the caption of their own plot as a length of stay rather than a data cut-off date, and may reuse the str_glue() pattern believing it computes a duration.

findings.heading: ggplot basics (introduction)
findings.proposition: The English says tidyverse-compatible formatting makes using ggplot2 and the tidyverse packages together very EFFECTIVE; the Turkish says it makes using many packages together OBLIGATORY ("zorunlu kılar").
findings.reader_consequence: The reader concludes ggplot2 cannot be used without adopting a set of other packages, which may deter them from using ggplot2 with base data structures.

findings.heading: Free or fixed axes
findings.proposition: The English gives "free" as the literal value to release both axes; the Turkish, in the same list as "free_x", tells the reader to write "serbest", which ggplot2 does not accept and which the adjacent chunk (scales = "free", tr 472) contradicts.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader writes scales = "serbest" to free both axes and the call fails, while the two neighbouring values ("free_y", "free_x") work, giving no clue why.

findings.heading: Box plots
findings.proposition: The English says geom_boxplot() creates a BOX plot; the Turkish body text says geom_boxplot() creates a bar chart ("çubuk grafiği"), the same term the chapter uses elsewhere for geom_bar()/geom_col() (tr 175, tr 985 onward).
findings.reader_consequence: The reader conflates box plots with bar charts, and within the same paragraph meets both "çubuk grafiği" and "kutu grafiği" for the same object, so they cannot tell which geom produces which figure.

findings.heading: Facets / Small-multiples
findings.proposition: The English says the quick faceting examples that follow use the malaria dataset, with a parenthetical link to the download page; the Turkish says to look at the "Download handbook and data" page FOR those examples.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader leaves the chapter to find worked examples on the download page, which holds only data-download instructions, and may miss that the examples are in the next few sections.

findings.heading: Histograms
findings.proposition: The English shows the stat_bin() console message in a plain fenced block, as the console output the prose promises; the Turkish wraps the same text in an executable R chunk carrying figure options (```{r fig.show='hold', out.width=c('50%','50%')}), so it renders as R source rather than as the message.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is told a message appears after the plot, then sees what looks like a runnable code chunk containing only a comment, so they may try to run it or take the message for code they must type.
